boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named CSUB places for studying, making, recharging, connecting, recreation, art, and campus activities, supported by current university sources.

cards.title: Find Your Study Mode at Stiern
cards.subtitle: Collaborative rooms and quieter upper levels
cards.notes: Use collaborative areas for group work, reserve a study room when available, or move upstairs when you need a quieter setting.
cards.short_summary: A five-level learning hub with spaces for both collaborative and focused work.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUB says the Walter W. Stiern Library offers collaborative spaces, group study rooms, and silent spaces on its upper levels.
cards.access_notes: Library access and room availability may follow current university schedules and reservation rules.

cards.title: Settle Into the Student Union Lounge
cards.subtitle: A shared place to meet, study, and reset
cards.notes: Bring a classmate to the central lounge, use the low tables for coursework, or check whether a laptop is available at the desk.
cards.short_summary: The campus living room combines casual seating, study surfaces, games, events, and student services.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUB describes the Student Union as a place where students meet, organize, attend events, study, read, play games, and converse.
cards.source_title: Student Union - The Hub of Student Life on Campus
cards.access_notes: Use during posted Student Union business hours; particular rooms and equipment may have separate availability rules.

cards.title: Schedule a Deliberate Reset
cards.subtitle: Nap pods, massage chairs, and meditation space
cards.notes: Head to the SRC’s second floor between classes; ask about reserving a nap pod or massage chair and keep the lounge atmosphere quiet.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated second-floor decompression space designed for rest and personal well-being.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUB states that the second-floor Wellness Suite has reservable nap pods and massage chairs, plus areas for lounging and meditation.
cards.access_notes: Located on the SRC second floor; ask staff about reservations and current facility access. Student access is covered through student fees.

cards.title: Try the SRC’s Indoor Climbing Wall
cards.subtitle: A staffed climbing space inside the recreation center
cards.notes: Bring your CSUB ID and ask the climbing staff how to begin; review current wall procedures before using ropes or auto-belays.
cards.short_summary: The SRC’s freestanding climbing wall offers a distinct indoor alternative to a standard workout.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUB identifies The Rock as a 34-foot freestanding wall with two auto-belays and five rope belays, accommodating up to seven roped climbers.
cards.access_notes: CSUB students need a CSUB ID for recreation-center access; follow current wall hours, staff instructions, and safety requirements.

cards.title: Play, Plan, or Unwind in the TEC
cards.subtitle: Gaming and community space below Stiern Library
cards.notes: Enter near the library’s west entrance, bring your ID, and use an open table to plan with friends or an available station to play.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level technology hub that supports gaming, creative work, and low-key social time.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUB calls the Technology Engagement Center a hub for gaming, creativity, and community and locates it on Stiern Library’s lower level near the west entrance.
cards.access_notes: A CSUB ID is indicated for the space. The official page says the TEC is closed in summer and posts separate fall hours.

cards.title: Turn a Digital Design Into an Object
cards.subtitle: Student-accessible fabrication in the Engineering Complex
cards.notes: Stop by during open hours with a project idea, then ask the specialist or student interns which machine and preparation steps fit it.
cards.short_summary: A campus makerspace equipped for laser cutting, 3D printing, and vinyl cutting.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUB says its Engineering Complex Fab Lab is open to students and the public, with laser cutters, 3D printers, vinyl cutters, and staff assistance.
cards.access_notes: Find it in the Engineering Complex north of Parking Lot H and visit during posted open hours; projects may involve material costs.

cards.title: Use the DRC’s Community Rooms
cards.subtitle: Lounges, libraries, snacks, and practical support in Rohan
cards.notes: Visit the Rohan Building and ask staff about the student lounges, community libraries, Monarch Community Space, or other available help.
cards.short_summary: A welcoming resource center with several concrete places to sit, connect, read, and obtain support.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUB lists student lounges and community libraries in rooms 112, 114, and 115, plus Monarch Community Space in room 118, among DRC services.
cards.source_title: Welcome to the Dreamers Resource Center
cards.access_notes: Located inside the Center for Identity and Belonging in the Rohan Building near Parking Lot E; use during posted center hours.

cards.title: Study Alongside Military-Connected Peers
cards.subtitle: A dedicated Modular West support space
cards.notes: If you are military-connected, stop in to study, meet peers, or ask staff about benefits, advising, and other campus resources.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated setting where eligible students can combine practical support with peer study and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUB documents that student veterans can study and collaborate with peers in a dedicated Veterans Success Center space while accessing advising and benefits information.
cards.access_notes: Located in Modular West beside the Children's Center; services and the dedicated space are intended for military-connected students.

cards.title: See What Is Showing Beside Doré Theatre
cards.subtitle: Campus exhibitions and student thesis work
cards.notes: Check the current-exhibit notice before walking over, then use the show as a conversation starter or a short creative break.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery where visiting artists and CSUB student thesis exhibitions share the same program.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUB says the Todd Madigan Art Gallery presents historical and contemporary artists, organizes Student Thesis shows, and brings visiting artists to campus.
cards.access_notes: Located next to the Frances B. Doré Theatre. Confirm the current exhibition and gallery schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Use Alumni Park as an Event Landmark
cards.subtitle: An outdoor gathering site for campus programming
cards.notes: Check the campus-programming calendar, meet friends at the named park, and bring sun protection for daytime outdoor activities.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable campus green used for welcome-week gatherings and other organized student activities.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUB’s Week of Welcome page identifies Alumni Park as the location for student activities, including a transfer social and the Wishing Tree event.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and scheduled uses vary; consult the current campus-programming calendar before planning around an event.
